findings.title: Unrestricted shell execution
findings.whyItMatters: Letting model or tool output reach a shell can turn a suggestion into local code execution.
findings.recommendedFix: Use structured commands, strict allowlists, argument arrays, and human approval before running mutating commands.

findings.title: Remote script piped into shell
findings.whyItMatters: Piping remote content directly into a shell bypasses review and can execute changed code without a local audit trail.
findings.recommendedFix: Download to a reviewed file, verify integrity, pin sources, and require human approval before execution.

findings.title: Agent approval disabled
findings.whyItMatters: Disabling approvals removes the human checkpoint that should protect repository writes, tool calls, and deployments.
findings.recommendedFix: Require approval for file writes, shell commands, package installs, network calls, pushes, merges, and deployments.

findings.title: Wildcard tool or file permission
findings.whyItMatters: Wildcard allow rules make it hard to reason about what an agent can read, write, or execute.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace wildcard permissions with named tools, scoped paths, and a deny list for secrets, build output, and repository metadata.

findings.title: Overly broad MCP or tool permission config
findings.evidence: MCP tool permissions: unrestricted filesystem, unrestricted shell, unrestricted browser.
findings.whyItMatters: Broad MCP permissions can expose filesystem, network, browser, or credential capabilities beyond what a repo task needs.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare the minimal MCP servers and tool calls needed, disable unused tools, and require approvals for sensitive capabilities.
